title: Best Private Search Engines Compared
metaDescription: Compare top private search engines like DuckDuckGo, Startpage, and Brave Search. Find the best anonymous search option for your privacy needs.
intro: Tired of Google tracking your every search? Private search engines give you good results without building profiles on you. This page compares four of them on privacy, result quality, ease of use and mobile support, and each rating is worked out from the table.

verdict.summary: On these four criteria DuckDuckGo scores highest, with a clean interface, instant answers and its own mobile browser app. Startpage is second: it shows Google-sourced results without passing your identity to Google. Brave Search comes third and runs its own independent index. SearXNG scores lowest here because result quality depends on the instance you use and the sources it draws on, but it's the only one you can host yourself.

pro_tips: Pair your private search engine with a browser that blocks trackers and clears its history: the search engine protects your searches, not the sites you visit afterwards.
Set your private search engine as the default in all browsers to avoid accidentally using Google out of habit.
Try different private search engines for different types of queries - use Startpage for news, DuckDuckGo for general searches.
Use search operators like site: and intitle: to improve results quality on private search engines.
Consider using multiple private search engines - if one doesn't find what you need, try another for different result sources.

faqs.question: Are private search engines as good as Google?
faqs.answer: For most everyday searches they work well, though they lack Google's personalization. Startpage shows Google's own results without passing your identity to Google.

faqs.question: Do private search engines make money without ads?
faqs.answer: Most private search engines do show ads, but they're based on your search terms rather than personal data. DuckDuckGo shows contextual ads, while others use affiliate partnerships or donations.

faqs.question: Will switching hurt my search experience?
faqs.answer: There's usually a brief adjustment period, but most users adapt quickly. The trade-off of slightly different results is worth the privacy benefits for most people.

faqs.question: Can I still use Google sometimes?
faqs.answer: Absolutely! You can use private search engines as your default while occasionally using Google for specific needs. Many users find they rarely need to go back.

faqs.question: Do private search engines work on mobile?
faqs.answer: Yes, all major private search engines have mobile-optimized websites and can be set as default search engines on mobile browsers. DuckDuckGo also offers a privacy-focused mobile browser.
